item.title: Rust SDK Adds Stable 2026-07-28 MCP Version with New Features
item.description:
Rust SDK Adds Stable 2026-07-28 MCP Version with New Features

This release brings the stable MCP 2026‑07‑28 specification to the Rust SDK, while remaining fully compatible with the 2025‑11‑25 release and earlier versions.

🔍 Overview

  • The SDK implements the stable MCP 2026-07-28 specification.
  • It remains fully compatible with the 2025-11-25 release and previous versions.

🧩 Features

  • Server discovery & negotiation
  • Transport‑neutral subscriptions
  • Long‑running tasks
  • Response caching
  • Multi‑round‑trip requests
  • Standard HTTP routing headers

⚙️ SDK Structure

  • Repository crates:
    • rmcp: core crate providing the RMCP protocol implementation
    • rmcp‑macros: procedural macro crate for generating RMCP tool implementations
  • Basic dependencies:
    • tokio
    • serde
  • JSON Schema generation (version 2020‑12):
    • schemars

📦 Installation & Setup

  • Add the latest published version: 
    1

    cargo add rmcp --features server
  • Or use the dev channel: 
    1

    cargo add rmcp --features server --git https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk --branch main

🚀 Server and Client Lifecycle

  • serve() uses the legacy MCP lifecycle:
    • The client sends initialize.
    • The server returns negotiated server information.
    • The client sends notifications/initialized.
  • Use ClientServiceExt::serve_with_lifecycle to select another lifecycle explicitly.
  • ClientLifecycleMode::Initialize is equivalent to the existing serve() behavior.
  • Discover startup does not send notifications/initialized; discovery completes startup.
  • Each subsequent request carries its protocol version, client information, and capabilities in _meta.
  • For a server, serve() waits for peer input that establishes the protocol lifecycle, such as initialize from a legacy client.
  • A stdio MCP server is normally launched by an MCP client as a child process.
  • Running the executable alone in a terminal can leave this await pending because no client has sent protocol messages yet.
  • After serve() returns, the service handles messages in the background.
  • You can run other asynchronous work, then use waiting() to wait for shutdown.
  • To cancel during startup, use serve_with_ct().

🛠️ Building a Service

  • Use ServerHandler or ClientHandler to build a service.
  • Await protocol startup, then receive a handle to the running service.

#Rust #MCP #SDK #Async #JSON

Source: modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk

item.title: Rust-Powered Multi-Protocol Download Manager Features Dynamic Acceleration and AI Agent Integration
item.description:
Rust-Powered Multi-Protocol Download Manager Features Dynamic Acceleration and AI Agent Integration

A new open-source download manager powered by Rust and the Tokio engine has been released as a free alternative to IDM. The tool features dynamic download acceleration with adaptive segmentation and is designed to be AI-agent ready through a built-in Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

🔍 Overview

The manager is a local-first, multi-protocol solution that requires no account for local downloads and contains zero advertisements. It uses a shared Rust + Tokio engine that remains independent of the UI and Foreign Function Interface (FFI), allowing it to power various client types from a single core.

  • Multi-protocol support: Handles HTTP/HTTPS, FTP, BitTorrent (including magnet links), eD2K, and streaming via HLS and DASH.
  • Cross-platform clients: Native GPUI desktop apps, Kotlin Android and SwiftUI iOS apps, a React Web UI, and a standalone CLI.
  • Browser integration: Includes a 3-layer interception engine for Chrome, Edge, and Firefox, supplemented by a userscript.

🧩 How it works

The engine implements dynamic download acceleration by splitting segments at runtime. If a segment is performing poorly, idle workers utilize a “slow-segment rescue” feature to take over the task. For persistence, the manager uses SQLite with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) by default to store resumable states, while server deployments have the option to use PostgreSQL.

Protocol Capabilities
BitTorrent Supports DHT, UPnP, and magnet links
eD2K / eMule Server and Kad DHT source finding with MD4 verification
HLS / DASH Streaming media sniffing and AES-decryption support
Automation RSS subscriptions, scheduled queues, and JavaScript plugins

⚙️ Key details

The software includes professional-grade management tools such as named queues, global token-bucket rate limiting, and connection diagnostics. For developers and power users, it provides several integration paths:

  • AI Readiness: A built-in MCP server with 12 tools allows Claude, Cursor, and other AI clients to manage downloads.
  • Remote Management: Optional FluxCloud device collaboration for settings sync, remote task management, and LAN device pairing.
  • API Support: Offers REST/OpenAPI and aria2-compatible JSON-RPC interfaces.
  • Privacy: Anonymous installation and daily-active statistics can be disabled via settings and do not collect task-specific information.

🚀 Availability

The manager is available across multiple platforms including Windows, macOS, Linux, NAS, and Android. The desktop version includes a system tray service to keep downloads active after the main UI is closed. Users can choose between native GPUI interfaces or a React-based web management console, both supporting light, dark, and custom themes.

#Rust #OpenSource #AIagents #MCP #DownloadManager

item.title: Stagehand released as an SDK for building and interacting with browser agents
item.description:
Stagehand released as an SDK for building and interacting with browser agents

Stagehand is an SDK released for building and interacting with browser agents. It allows developers to extract data and interact with any site on the web.

🧩 How it works

Stagehand is designed to manage browser sessions efficiently by handling persistence and security:

  • Security: The observe() method returns real selectors, ensuring that credentials never reach the model.

The SDK provides specific methods for interacting with web interfaces, with each function serving a distinct purpose:

Method Function
act() Self-heals when the site redesigns its form.
extract() Returns schema-validated data.
observe() Returns real selectors so credentials never reach the model.

💡 Why it matters

The tool enables developers to sign in once, keep the session, and pull structured data out the other side. This workflow supports reliable automation by maintaining state between runs and validating the data returned by the agent.

item.title: Understanding AI Coordination Patterns
item.description:
Understanding AI Coordination Patterns

AI coordination patterns are crucial for effective multi-agent systems. When early implementations fall short, the cause is rarely the model.

🔍 Overview

  • Multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem.
  • ~88% of AI pilots never reach production.
  • Two models can perform worse collaborating than either alone when coordination overhead exceeds the benefit.
  • Teams are adding complexity faster than they build understanding.
  • Ten steps that are each 95 percent reliable deliver only 59.9 percent end-to-end reliability.
  • 20 steps deliver 35.8 percent.
  • Each dependent handoff multiplies risk.

🧩 How it works

Coordination patterns fall into two tiers, based on who controls the flow.

Tier 1: Patterns (deterministic control flow)

  • Sequential Pipeline: Orchestration patterns that implement linear execution where each node’s output feeds into the next node (A -> B -> C) supporting ordered processing with predictable execution timing.
  • Conditional Workflow: Logic-based edges select the next node by condition, so the workflow can branch and send each case down a different path.
  • Conditional Router: A classification step examines the input and directs it to the appropriate processing path. Only one path is executed per request.
  • Parallel Workflow: A task splits into independent subtasks that run simultaneously across handlers, each on its own data. A fan-in step combines the results when all handlers complete, and a failure in one path retries only that path.

Tier 2: Autonomous patterns (LLM-determined control flow)

  • In autonomous patterns, control flow is determined at runtime by the AI model itself, not predefined by developers.
  • Plan-based orchestration: In plan-based orchestration, a single orchestrator agent acts as a project manager.
    • The orchestrator maintains an explicit task plan with assignments and dependencies, sees all context while each worker receives only its slice, distributes work dynamically against the current plan, and monitors progress centrally.
    • Key design choice is that the workers are stateless and independent. If one fails, it doesn’t contaminate others.
    • The orchestrator retries only the failed worker, not the entire workflow.
  • Handoff pattern: Agents operate with limited, local knowledge and coordinate through peer-to-peer delegation.
    • Each makes local decisions about when and to whom to transfer control, based on the task and the agents it knows.
    • Control passes with state: each transfer carries validated task state, the evidence behind it, and any unresolved questions, so the receiving agent continues rather than reinterpreting a summary.

💡 Why it matters

  • The practical default is to start with Tier 1 and move a task to Tier 2 only when its subtasks emerge during the work.

#AICoordination #MultiAgentSystems #AIAgents #DistributedSystems

Source: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing | Amazon Web Services

item.title: Datasette Progresses Toward 1.0 Milestone with CSS View Transitions and Streaming Support
item.description:
Datasette Progresses Toward 1.0 Milestone with CSS View Transitions and Streaming Support

On November 15, 2026, developers shared updates on the progress of the Datasette 1.0 milestone, which is now 53% complete. The latest release includes significant architectural changes, security patches, and user interface enhancements developed with assistance from Claude Fable 5.2.

⚙️ Key details

The release introduces several functional improvements to the platform’s core data handling and display capabilities:

  • Streaming Support: Output renderers, including built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms, now utilize streaming.
  • Plugin API: A new Response.stream() method allows plugins to register as capable of streaming every row in a table in a single operation.
  • JSON Redesign: The row page JSON representation has been redesigned for the 1.0 standard, and JSON data within columns can now be pretty-printed.
  • UI Components: A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component has been added to provide copy-schema functionality in various locations.

🧩 How it works

A major feature in this release is the implementation of CSS multi-page view transitions, which allow the multi-page application to behave more like a single-page application (SPA).

Component Mechanism
.facet-results Morphs from old position to new position during transition.
.table-wrapper Morphs position if it contains .rows-and-columns.
DatasetteModal.confirm() A new JavaScript utility method for handling confirmations.

These transitions are enabled for users who do not have “prefers-reduced-motion” active. This functionality currently works in Safari and Chrome.

🛡️ Security and Improvements

This update addresses dozens of bugs and includes a specific security fix regarding private stored queries. A GitHub advisory was issued because private stored queries could previously be exposed, revealing the title and SQL of the query, though they could not be executed by unauthorized parties.

General bug fixes were supported by several contributors, including:

  • Zihan Dai
  • Peter Olkhovets
  • Ilya Khalafi
  • Ankita Advitot

🚀 Availability

While currently available for Safari and Chrome users, Firefox support for the new CSS view transitions is expected to arrive on December 8th, 2026, with the release of Firefox 162. These features are no longer feature-flagged in Firefox Nightly.

#Datasette #OpenSource #WebDevelopment

Source: Release: datasette 1.0a43

item.title: E2B Desktop Sandbox Enables Secure AI-Driven Computer Use
item.description:
E2B Desktop Sandbox Enables Secure AI-Driven Computer Use

E2B Desktop Sandbox introduces an open‑source secure virtual desktop that can be connected to any large language model for safe computer interactions.

🔍 Overview

  • E2B Desktop Sandbox is an open source secure virtual desktop ready for Computer Use.
  • It offers a desktop graphical environment that can connect to any LLM for secure computer use.
  • The sandbox is built on top of E2B Sandbox.

🧩 How it Works

  • Each sandbox is isolated from the others and can be customized with any dependencies you want.
  • The sandbox template and example code are maintained in this repository.
  • SDK sources for JavaScript and Python are now in the E2B monorepo under packages/desktop-js and packages/desktop-python.
  • Authentication uses an auto‑generated key; you can retrieve the authentication key.
  • Set the environment variable E2B_API_KEY with your API key.
  • Only one stream is allowed at a time:
    • Stop the current stream before starting another.
    • An error is raised if the desired application is not open.
    • The stream closes automatically when the application closes.
    • Multiple streams cannot run simultaneously.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Powered by E2B.
  • The OpenAI Computer Use Agent uses E2B’s Desktop Sandbox.
  • The system runs as a Next.js app.
  • Computer use is achieved with 100% open source LLMs.

🚀 Availability

💡 Why it Matters

E2B Desktop Sandbox provides a secure, isolated environment for AI agents to interact with a computer system, ensuring safe and controlled usage across diverse applications.

item.title: Kiro Crew Offers a Persistent, Self-Evolving Development Workspace
item.description:
Kiro Crew Offers a Persistent, Self-Evolving Development Workspace

Kiro Crew is an open-source development workspace that runs locally or remotely on your hardware, with work designed to persist, learn, and evolve beyond a single session.

🔍 Overview

You can work with Kiro Crew through a desktop app, web dashboard, or CLI, and continue the same work through connection tools such as Slack and Discord.

🧩 How it works

  • Multi-step tasks can run unattended.
  • Recurring jobs run on a schedule.
  • Heartbeats monitor systems until something needs attention.
  • Kiro Crew Apps adapt the workspace to a specific job, combining a purpose-built interface with agents, skills, schedules, integrations, and backend services.

⚙️ Setup and updates

Kiro Crew can be run in several ways:

  • Use the desktop app, which includes automatic updates.
  • Install it on a machine or remote host with a one-line install.
  • Use the Docker image for always-on servers.
  • Build it from source.

The default agent runs on kiro-cli, which must be installed and signed in to separately. On first launch, Kiro Crew checks for this prerequisite and links to the official setup guide if it is missing. Download links fetch the newest build on their channel, and the app updates itself on that same channel. The recommended channel is Stable unless there is a reason to choose another.

🚀 Availability

Kiro Crew is available for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Package options include:

Platform Package
macOS (Apple Silicon or Intel) .dmg
Windows (x64) .exe
Linux (x86_64 or aarch64) .deb, .rpm, or AppImage

On Linux, the one-line install is the recommended starting point; a desktop package can be added for a native window and in-app updates.

#KiroCrew #AIAgents #OpenSource #DevTools

item.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Architecture Debuts in MLPerf Training v6.1
item.description:
NVIDIA Vera Rubin Architecture Debuts in MLPerf Training v6.1

NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin architecture has made its debut in MLPerf Training v6.1, showcasing impressive performance and scalability. The new architecture, along with its CUDA software stack, has demonstrated significant advancements in AI training capabilities.

🔍 Overview

  • MLPerf Training v6.1 marks the debut of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin architecture.
  • Vera Rubin NVL72 platform delivered the fastest time to train on six of the seven benchmarks.
  • NVIDIA platforms hold the fastest time to train on every benchmark in v6.1.
  • Vera Rubin successfully completed the entire suite in its inaugural run.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Vera Rubin NVL72 achieved up to 2x more performance than a highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 baseline.
  • For the DeepSeek-V3 671B benchmark, NVIDIA demonstrated massive scale on a 10,240-GPU GB300 NVL72 cluster.
  • Vera Rubin maintained above 97% overall efficiency when scaling from 256 to 1,024 GPUs.
  • NVIDIA platforms were the only ones to submit results across all seven benchmarks.

🚀 Availability

  • The Vera Rubin architecture is now available and has been tested in MLPerf Training v6.1.

💡 Why it Matters

  • The performance gains span the entire modeling pipeline, supporting everything from large-scale pretraining to reinforcement learning post-training.
  • The new architecture is designed to handle the most demanding workloads, including the 671-billion-parameter token-dropless Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model.
  • The Vera Rubin platform also proved its flexibility by submitting on two different inference backends: NVIDIA NeMo RL with TensorRT-LLM and with vLLM.
  • The NVIDIA Vera CPU is integral to the architecture, sustaining more than 22,500 concurrent RL environments across 256 CPUs in a single Vera CPU rack.

#NVIDIA #VeraRubin #MLPerf #AITraining #CUDA #DeepLearning

Source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Achieves up to 2x Blackwell Ultra Performance in MLPerf Training v6.1 | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: Python SDK for Model Context Protocol Released
item.description:
Python SDK for Model Context Protocol Released

The official Python SDK for Model Context Protocol servers and clients has been released, providing a Python implementation of the Model Context Protocol (MCP). The documentation is available at https://py.sdk.modelcontextprotocol.io/, including a Get started guide, What’s new in v2, the API reference, and a migration guide.

🔍 Overview

  • The Model Context Protocol lets you build servers that expose data and functionality to LLM applications in a secure, standardized way.
  • Think of it like a web API, but designed for LLM interactions.

🧩 How it works

  • Build MCP servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts to any MCP host.
  • Build MCP clients that connect to any MCP server.
  • Speak every standard transport: stdio, Streamable HTTP, and SSE.
  • Python 3.11+ is required.

⚙️ Key details

  • The cli extra adds the mcp command-line tool (mcp dev, mcp run, mcp install) on top of the SDK; install plain mcp if you don’t need it.
  • For one-off commands, uv run --with "mcp[cli]" mcp ... works without a project.
  • Example usage: Add two numbers or greet someone by name.
  • That’s a complete MCP server: one tool, one templated resource.
  • Call add with a=1, b=2 and you get 3 back.
  • Notice what you did not write: no JSON Schema (a: int, b: int is the schema), no request parsing, no validation code, no protocol handling.
  • Two type-hinted Python functions and a docstring.
  • The same package is a full MCP client.
  • A URL means Streamable HTTP, the transport you deploy.
  • Client can also launch a local server as a stdio subprocess or take any custom transport.

🚀 Availability

  • The project is licensed under the MIT License.
  • Contributions are welcome; see the contributing guide to get started.

💡 Why it matters

  • The SDK simplifies building and connecting to MCP servers and clients, reducing the need for manual request parsing, validation, and protocol handling.
  • It supports various transports, making it versatile for different deployment scenarios.
  • The project aims to support contributors of all levels of experience.

#PythonSDK #ModelContextProtocol #LLMApplications #AITools

Source: modelcontextprotocol/python-sdk

item.title: Security Update Resolves Unauthorized Access in Database Registration Routing
item.description:
Security Update Resolves Unauthorized Access in Database Registration Routing

A minor security fix has been backported from version 1.0a43 to address a vulnerability that allowed unauthorized database downloads. This update resolves a security issue occurring when database routes and names do not match.

⚙️ Key details

  • Affected Registration: The issue involves databases registered using add_database(db, name=..., route=...).
  • Vulnerability Condition: The security flaw occurred when a database was registered with a route that differed from its name.
  • Access Restriction Bypass: In these instances, actors who were denied access to the database could still download it from the /<route>.db endpoint.

🚀 Availability

  • The security fix was backported from version 1.0a43.

#Cybersecurity #Database #SoftwarePatch

Source: Release: datasette 0.65.6

item.title: Synadia Agent Protocol Connects AI Agents Through NATS
item.description:
Synadia Agent Protocol Connects AI Agents Through NATS

The Synadia Agent Protocol for NATS lets AI agents register as agents micro services that callers can discover, prompt, and stream from using the same wire format. The project includes TypeScript and Python caller and host SDKs, along with pre-built plugins for connecting existing AI harnesses to NATS.

🔍 How it works

  • Each agent registers as an agents micro service and serves the protocol’s prompt, status, and hb endpoints.
  • Subjects follow the pattern agents.{verb}.{token}.{owner}.{session}, where verb is prompt, hb, or status.
  • The protocol can be used with Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code, OpenClaw, PI, Hermes, Flue, or a custom agent.

🧩 SDKs and plugins

The SDKs are split into caller and host packages in both TypeScript and Python:

Component Role
Caller SDK (client-sdk/) Discovers and prompts agents.
Host SDK (agent-sdk/) Registers and serves an agent.

Caller-only consumers install the caller package; authors hosting agents install both halves of their language’s pair. A cross-SDK interoperability test runs the TypeScript reference agent against the Python client to validate the shared wire format.

Pre-built channel plugins connect existing AI harnesses to NATS without writing code. The active SDK release rollout roadmap tracks sender identity, extension hooks, compatibility, integration adoption, dependency controls, and release promotion.

⚙️ Extensions and applications

Tracing is not part of this release. The SDKs provide generic extension hooks, including prompt and request interceptors, extra envelope fields, and heartbeat extras; tracing extensions can be built in separate packages.

Apps built on the SDKs include:

  • A Vue 3 browser client for discovery, prompting with attachments, streaming, and inline mid-stream query allow or deny.
  • A control plane that spawns sessions when it discovers a headless controller and fans a single prompt across multiple working directories in parallel.
  • A process that spawns and manages headless Claude Code sessions, each registering as a first-class agent at agents.prompt.cc-headless.<owner>.<session>.

#NATS #AIAgents #AgentProtocol #TypeScript #Python

Source: synadia-ai/synadia-agents

item.title: Datasette-Leaflet plugin updates tile request referrer policy
item.description:
Datasette-Leaflet plugin updates tile request referrer policy

On 13th November 2026, an update was released for the datasette-leaflet plugin to ensure compliance with OpenStreetMap’s tile server policy regarding referrer headers.

⚙️ Key details

  • OpenStreetMap requires that requests to their hosted tile server include a referrer header.
  • Previously, Datasette table pages used the Referrer-Policy: no-referrer HTTP header, which caused plugins loading tiles from OpenStreetMap to violate this policy.
  • Datasette-leaflet is a plugin that bundles Leaflet for use by other Datasette plugins.

💡 Why it matters

  • The plugin now explicitly sets the referrer policy on tile requests to strict-origin-when-cross-origin.
  • This update allows the host information to be passed while withholding the full path to the page, satisfying OpenStreetMap requirements.

#Datasette #OpenStreetMap #Leaflet #WebDevelopment #HTTP

Source: Release: datasette-leaflet 0.3

item.title: Deploying NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard with LiteLLM on AWS
item.description:
Deploying NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard with LiteLLM on AWS

LiteLLM now includes a native built-in Switchyard stage router, allowing developers to route AI model requests through an open source gateway. By using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK), you can deploy this configuration on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate.

🧩 How it works

Switchyard acts as a routing plugin that allows an AI agent to choose which model handles each request. The integration functions by sending an OpenAI-compatible request with the model field set to the specific LiteLLM model group. The system operates on Amazon Bedrock using the Converse or ConverseStream API.

⚙️ Key details

  • Routing Strategies: The plugin supports Stage routing (choosing between two candidates) and Random routing (traffic splits via weight for A/B comparisons).
  • Infrastructure: The setup uses an Application Load Balancer, AWS WAF for request filtering, and Amazon Route 53 for hostname resolution.
  • Security: AWS Secrets Manager handles gateway keys, and the task security group limits access strictly to the load balancer.
  • Monitoring: Logs are maintained in Amazon CloudWatch for 30 days, with metrics collected via Container Insights.

🛠 Routing Strategies

Strategy Requirements Function
Stage Exactly two candidates Picks between a capable model and a lower-cost efficient model
Random At least two candidates Picks from configured models using optional weights

Note: Classifier-backed strategies, such as Task and Composite routing, require intermediate model calls that this integration does not support.

#AWS #LiteLLM #NVIDIA #AI #LLM

Source: Route coding agent requests to the right model on Amazon Bedrock with NVIDIA NeMo Switchyard | Amazon Web Services

item.title: CLI tool adds automated scoring and checklist for Agent projects
item.description:
CLI tool adds automated scoring and checklist for Agent projects

The agent-handbook project released a new CLI tool that can automatically score an Agent codebase against a five‑pillar checklist drawn from its 31‑chapter Chinese handbook.

🔍 Overview

  • Provides a static scan of your Agent project and reports which of the five pillars are missing.
  • Maps gaps to the exact chapter and section of the handbook that explains the concept.
  • Generates a 0–10 score with concrete remediation suggestions.

🛠️ How it works

  • The command handbook doctor . walks the code, checks it against the five‑pillar criteria, and produces a Markdown table of results.
  • --md flag outputs the table so it can be pasted directly into an issue, README, or PR comment; the tool also posts the report automatically to the PR and the Job Summary.
  • handbook search <keyword> performs full‑text search across all 31 chapters, returning chapter, line number, and snippet.
  • handbook new <name> scaffolds a new Agent project that already satisfies all five pillars, earning a full score.
  • The tool runs with zero dependencies, using only the Python standard library, and works offline because the handbook data is bundled with the package.

⚙️ Key details

Command Description
handbook doctor . Five‑pillar health check, 0–10 score + remediation suggestions
handbook doctor . --md Output Markdown table for easy inclusion in issues/README
handbook search 上下文压缩 Full‑text search of the 31‑chapter handbook, returns chapter, line, snippet
handbook new my-agent Generate an Agent skeleton that scores full on the five pillars
Chapter Title Quick note
00 新手快速入门 10 分钟跑通第一个 Agent
03 LangGraph 图编排 复杂工作流、状态机、检查点
04 CrewAI 多智能体 角色化团队、任务分配
06 LlamaIndex RAG 文档检索、向量数据库
07 Dify 低代码 可视化拖拽构建应用
11 MCP 协议 标准化工具连接（含 2026 无状态核心）
14 记忆系统与状态管理 Mem0、向量记忆、持久化
16 调试与可观测性 LangSmith、日志、追踪
19 Agent 通用工具箱 工具注册中心 / 审批网关 / 成本追踪等六件套
20 Codex CLI MCP 集成、四种审批模式、沙箱隔离
21 DeepSeek Harness 四种模式、SWE‑bench、500+ 插件
23 Aider 代码助手 多模型、Git 集成、会话恢复
25 Harness Engineering 五支柱：2026 年 Agent 上生产的分水岭
30 Agent 评测体系 EDD、三层评测金字塔
99 中英对照术语表 130+ 术语通俗解释

🚀 Availability

  • Install with zero‑install uvx: uvx agent-handbook doctor .
  • Alternative: pipx run agent-handbook doctor .
  • Or install via pip: pip install agent-handbook
  • The handbook chapters are packaged together, so the tool works fully offline.

💡 Why it matters

  • Turns the handbook’s methodology into a concrete, checkable checklist for developers.
  • Provides immediate, actionable feedback directly in the code review workflow.
  • Low barrier to entry: no external dependencies, works offline, and integrates with common CI/PR systems.
  • Supports rapid prototyping (handbook new) and ongoing quality monitoring (handbook doctor).

#AIAgents #CLI #AgentHandbook #DevTools

Source: Xwh630/ai-agent-handbook

item.title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen as New Free Tier and Search Model
item.description:
Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen as New Free Tier and Search Model

On 12th November 2026, Google launched Gemini 4 Hydrogen, the lowest cost member of the Gemini 4 family. Designed as a high-efficiency execution engine, the model is intended for everyday work and to power AI features within Google Search.

⚙️ Key details

Google describes Hydrogen’s position in their model lineup as a tool for fast, disciplined execution.

  • Model Roles: While teams use Carbon and Argon for deep architectural judgment and designing systems, Hydrogen is built for writing code, running tests, and verifying changes.
  • Workflow Integration: Hydrogen can stand alone for everyday tasks or pair with Carbon and Argon in multi-model workflows.
  • Capabilities: In a comparison of image generation, there is a stark difference in pelican quality for Hydrogen compared to its siblings.
Model Primary Function Performance Notes
Gemini 4 Hydrogen Everyday work, code execution, free tier Intended for fast, disciplined execution
Gemini 4 Carbon Architectural judgment, untangling bugs Frontier model
Gemini 4 Argon Architectural judgment, system design Faster responses and lower token spend than Carbon

💰 Pricing

The pricing for the Gemini 4 family is scheduled to change significantly in the coming month:

  • Current Rates: Hydrogen is currently priced at a 25% discount compared to Carbon and Argon. Carbon and Argon are currently the same price.
  • Scheduled Increases: On December 1st, the price of Carbon and Argon is scheduled to double.
  • Future Discount: After December 1st, the Hydrogen price will represent a 75% discount relative to its more capable peers.
  • Market Comparison: At 15x the cost of Claude Haiku 5.5 and GPT-6 Luna (which are both $0.10/$0.50), Hydrogen remains considerably more expensive than competing low-cost models.

🚀 Availability

Hydrogen is available immediately as the new model for Google’s free tier. It is also the specific model designated to power AI features in Google Search.

#Google #Gemini4 #ArtificialIntelligence #MachineLearning #SearchAI

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, efficient AI model for developers
item.description:
Google launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a fast, efficient AI model for developers

Today Google announced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a new model in the Gemini 4 family built for rapid, efficient execution of everyday coding and agentic workflows.

🔍 Overview

  • Hydrogen targets “rapid execution across diverse agentic workflows” while Carbon and Argon remain the frontier models for deep, long‑horizon reasoning.
  • It runs on a flat‑rate pricing of $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across a 1 million‑token context window (both input and output).
  • Four thinking levels – low, medium, high (default), and xhigh – let users trade quality, latency, and cost predictably.
  • The model pairs native 1 M‑token input with up to 1 M‑token output to synthesize dense PDFs, spreadsheets, charts, audio, and video into cited reports.

🧩 How it works

  • Hydrogen batches file‑read and search calls in parallel, enabling 2×‑2.8× faster repository exploration and 12%‑23% lower token usage compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash.
  • In multi‑step research or code‑base navigation it ranks #5 on Agent Arena and leads its class on HLE‑Diamond (58.8%), Vals Tax Agent Bench (52.3% #1), Vals Legal Research Bench (55.8% tied #1), and AutomationBench‑AA.
  • On the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent benchmark it scores 53.4%, and on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1 it scores 71.6%.
  • For developer‑centric tasks like live UI prototyping, design‑to‑code iteration, and interactive app building, Hydrogen generates more functional layouts with fewer prompts.

⚙️ Key details

Model Primary strength
Gemini 4 Carbon Deep, long‑horizon reasoning
Gemini 4 Argon Deep, long‑horizon reasoning
Gemini 4 Hydrogen Rapid, high‑throughput execution
  • Orchestrator (in Google Antigravity) automatically switches between models in a session. On Terminal‑Bench 4.0 it achieved near‑Carbon success rates while using 24% less quota and finishing 19% faster.
  • In multi‑agent workflows Carbon can coordinate while Hydrogen powers worker and verifier agents, allowing parallel development across isolated workspaces.
  • Compared with Gemini 3.8 Flash, Hydrogen finishes tasks 2.5× faster at its high default setting, more than triples Terminal‑Bench 4.1 scores (57% vs 18.2%), and reduces fabricated claims by >5×.

🚀 Availability

  • Hydrogen is available to all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for Business, the Gemini app, Google Search, and to paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google Antigravity.

💡 Why it matters

  • Teams can keep Carbon or Argon for deep architectural judgment while using Hydrogen as a disciplined execution engine for code writing, testing, and verification.
  • The lower latency and token‑efficient batching cut costs and speed up shipping of complex projects.
  • Improved instruction following, tone adherence, and tool‑calling make Hydrogen a reliable everyday assistant for drafting emails, study guides, and other documents.

#GoogleAI #Gemini #AIModels

Source: Introducing Gemini 4 Hydrogen

item.title: Hugging Face Releases llama.cpp v1.0.0 and ggml v1.0.0 Libraries
item.description:
Hugging Face Releases llama.cpp v1.0.0 and ggml v1.0.0 Libraries

The llama.cpp team at Hugging Face has released v1.0.0 of both the llama.cpp and ggml libraries, marking a significant milestone 3.5 years after the project’s inception.

🔍 Overview

With growing adoption and many downstream applications depending on the project, version 1.0.0 establishes a flexible and stable API standard. Moving forward, both llama.cpp and ggml, alongside all ggml-org projects using semantic versioning, will reflect API and ABI incompatibilities with major-version bumps.

⚙️ Released Libraries

Library Function
llama.cpp v1.0.0 LLM inference in C/C++
ggml v1.0.0 Tensor library for machine learning

🧩 How it works

llama.cpp makes it possible to run multi-modal LLMs across hardware ranging from consumer-grade local machines to high-end enterprise servers.

  • Inference Accessibility: Uses quantization, optimized backends, and a portable C/C++ implementation to deliver accessible AI inference across the software stack.
  • Dynamic Backends: ggml implements dedicated backends that can be compiled as dynamic libraries and optionally loaded at runtime to run on virtually any hardware.
  • Hardware Collaborations: Features hardware support and self-hosted runners from NVIDIA, AMD, Qualcomm, Arm, IBM, and Intel.
  • Model Compatibility: Supports continuous integration for all model architectures, currently covering over 150 architecture variants alongside mainstream speculative decoding methods.

🛠️ Infrastructure and Quality

  • Development priorities include maintaining a high-quality codebase, staying in control of the architecture, and understanding implementation details.
  • CI infrastructure uses Hugging Face technologies such as HF Buckets and HF Jobs to scale capacity and guarantee correctness for changes landing on master branches.
  • The team continues to thoughtfully integrate LLMs into its own development cycle.

🚀 Availability

  • Llama desktop applications are available for MacOS and Windows, shipped by the llama.cpp team and Hugging Face.
  • The team plans to expand software distribution methods to reach more developers and end-users.

#llamacpp #ggml #HuggingFace #OpenSourceAI #MachineLearning

item.title: Researchers Develop COMPACTIONBENCH and APEC to Reduce AI Coding Costs
item.description:
Researchers Develop COMPACTIONBENCH and APEC to Reduce AI Coding Costs

A new study reveals that while fewer than 8% of coding sessions require context compaction, these sessions account for 44% of total AI processing costs. To address this, researchers have introduced tools to optimize long-running coding tasks.

🧩 How it works

Researchers developed two primary solutions to manage context compaction more efficiently:

  • COMPACTIONBENCH: A benchmark designed to evaluate context compaction during long-running coding tasks.
  • APEC: A method that prepares summaries in the background, preventing the interruption of an agent’s work.

⚙️ Key details

Evaluations of the APEC method demonstrate measurable improvements in efficiency for coding agents:

Metric Improvement
Coding Performance Improved
Costs Reduced by up to 25.4%
Execution Time Reduced by 9.6%

#AI #Coding #MachineLearning #Efficiency

Source: Microsoft Research Focus – Edition #98 - Microsoft Research

item.title: Trustabl Introduces Open-Source Agent Reliability Analyzer for AI Agent Code
item.description:
Trustabl Introduces Open-Source Agent Reliability Analyzer for AI Agent Code

Trustabl’s Agent Reliability Analyzer is an open-source, deterministic scanner designed to find and fix reliability failures in AI agent code before it reaches production.

🔍 Overview

The Agent Reliability Analyzer performs deterministic static analysis across agent code to locate and resolve potential production failures. It operates entirely on your local machine without requiring a cloud scanner, an account, code uploads, or an LLM.

🧩 How it works

The tool scans an agent repository for gaps that break agents in production and applies fixes directly to the source code with a single command.

It detects specific vulnerabilities and failure points, including:

  • Tool descriptions that are too vague for a model to determine when to use them
  • Missing retry and timeout handling
  • Untyped parameters
  • Absent guardrails
  • Tool grants that exceed what the agent claims to do

⚙️ Key details

As of October 2026, the analyzer includes the following coverage metrics and architecture specs:

Feature Details
Rules 340+ rules
SDKs 9 SDKs
Languages 7 languages
Scopes 5 scopes
Engine Structure One agent reliability engine, ten front doors

🚀 Execution and installation

Scanning runs locally using standard commands:

  • Run directly via Docker: docker run --rm -v "$PWD:/repo" ghcr.io/trustabl/trustabl:latest scan /repo
  • Install via Homebrew: brew install trustabl/tap/trustabl

💡 Why it matters

While traditional scanners generate report files, Trustabl applies patches directly to the source code. This approach follows the design principle that reliability is engineered before deployment rather than observed after deployment.

#Trustabl #AIAgents #StaticAnalysis #OpenSource #SoftwareTesting

Source: trustabl/agent-reliability-analyzer

item.title: LLM 0.37 addresses security vulnerabilities in API key handling
item.description:
LLM 0.37 addresses security vulnerabilities in API key handling

🔍 Overview

On 11th November 2026, a security update was released for LLM to address two vulnerabilities reported by Daniel de Araujo in GHSA-v9h7-jj4g-f862 and GHSA-r639-rr7r-x72w.

⚙️ Key details

The security issues involved the accidental transmission of configured OpenAI API keys to external providers when using OpenAI-compatible API endpoints. The report identified two specific scenarios where this exposure could occur:

  • When a key named by api_key_name had not been previously stored.
  • When a ‘responses: true’ model was executed with the ‘-o chat_completions 1’ flag.

🧩 How it works

LLM utilizes a mechanism known as ’extra-openai-models.yaml’ to facilitate the use of OpenAI-compatible API endpoints from other providers. This mechanism is now managed by the new ’llm openai endpoint add’ command introduced in version 0.37.

#LLM #Security #OpenAI #API

Source: Release: llm 0.37.2

⚙️ Key details

07 Retired model

🛠️ How to adapt the course

  • Delete temperature and max_tokens from the llm_config; GPT‑5 models use the default temperature and max_completion_tokens instead of max_tokens.
  • Use substitute models listed on the OpenAI deprecations page; for small demos gpt-5.4-mini costs $0.75 / $4.50 per 1 M input/output tokens (cheaper than gpt-5.6-terra and gpt-5.6-sol).

item.title: Anthropic Releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2
item.description:
Anthropic Releases Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2

Anthropic has announced the availability of two new AI models, Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2, designed to address daunting technical challenges across software engineering, reasoning, and the sciences. Following the release of Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1 in September, the new 5.2 models offer faster output generation and are available on Amazon Bedrock and the Claude Platform on AWS.

🔍 Overview

Model Target Use Cases & Availability
Claude Fable 5.2 Generally available model for technical work, software engineering, math, and science. Designed to tackle long-running projects and orchestrate agent teams.
Claude Mythos 5.2 Specialized model for advanced cybersecurity and life sciences work. Available exclusively to vetted organizations through verification programs.

⚙️ Key Details and Performance

  • Capabilities: Shows marked improvements in coding, reasoning, and vision over previous versions. It takes on ambiguous, multi-step work, verifies its own output, catches errors, and optimizes while running unattended for hours to days.
  • Prerelease Benchmarks: During testing, the models completed otherwise-infeasible software migrations, designed three working electronic devices from scratch, solved two open theoretical physics problems related to black holes, made progress on robotics evaluations, and formalized the proof of Fermat’s Last Theorem in 30 hours.
  • Alignment Improvements: In Anthropic testing, Mythos 5.2 hallucinates less, completes tasks more reliably, surfaces key information consistently, and self-reports issues more honestly than Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, and Mythos 5.1. Fable 5.2 is expected to perform similarly.
  • Reasoning Behavior: When tested using command-line tools like llm-anthropic, setting reasoning effort to maximum caused the model to spend 128,000 tokens thinking without returning an output image, a behavior also observed in Opus 5.5.

🛡️ Data Retention and Security Controls

  • Covered Model Designation: Fable 5.2 defaults to requiring up to 30 days of data retention and human safety reviews performed by Amazon personnel within the AWS boundary on Amazon Bedrock.
  • Data Retention Settings: Users must enable the aws_review data retention mode on their account or project before invoking the model.
  • Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS): Combines zero data retention (ZDR) with misuse detection safeguards. Eligible customers can access zero data retention through June 30, 2027, while a version allowing customer-managed buckets and keys remains in development.
  • Fallback and Retry Rules: If a cybersecurity prompt is declined, it can be retried on Opus 4.8; declined biology queries can be retried on Opus 5. Retries on Amazon Bedrock must be implemented in application code. Requests declined at the prompt cache include a fallback credit token, ensuring retries are billed only as cache reads.

🚀 Availability and Setup

  • Amazon Bedrock Console: Accessible via Test > Playground by selecting Fable 5.2.
  • Programmatic Access: Can be invoked using the Anthropic Messages API against bedrock-runtime via the Anthropic SDK, or through the Invoke and Converse APIs via the AWS CLI and AWS SDK.
  • Prerequisites: Python 3.9 or later, Boto3 (pip install boto3), and IAM permissions for bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream.

#Anthropic #Claude #AmazonBedrock #ArtificialIntelligence #SoftwareEngineering

Source: Anthropic launches new Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 models Source: Introducing Claude Fable 5.2 on AWS | Amazon Web Services Source: Release: llm-anthropic 0.31

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 Performance on Coding Tasks Varies Based on Code Ownership Prompts
item.description:
Claude Fable 5.2 Performance on Coding Tasks Varies Based on Code Ownership Prompts

Anthropic’s testing of Claude Fable 5.2 reveals that the model responds closely to instructions regarding who owns the code it is tasked with modifying.

🧩 How it works

In testing involving small coding tasks, the model’s behavior changed based on the prompt’s description of ownership:

  • When prompts said nothing about ownership or presented the codebase as someone else’s, the model tended to add to the existing structure, even if it meant repeating existing code.
  • If the prompt stated the code belonged to the model, it was more likely to improve the structure while working.

⚙️ Key details

Anthropic found that using a specific sentence can trigger structural improvements: “This codebase is yours: what it’s for and how it’s built are your call, and you’ll keep building on it.”

Prompt Condition Frequency of Merging Repeated Code
With ownership sentence About half of the tries
Without ownership sentence Under a tenth of the tries

💡 Why it matters

The model’s tendency to merge repeated code increased significantly when it was told it owned the codebase. This suggests that explicit ownership instructions encourage Claude Fable 5.2 to reorganize and refine code structures rather than simply adding onto them.

#ClaudeFable #Anthropic #AICoding

Source: A quote from Prompting Claude Fable 5.2

item.title: Claude Opus 5.5 Generates Vanilla JS WebGL 3D Code Without Three.js
item.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 Generates Vanilla JS WebGL 3D Code Without Three.js

On 9 November 2026 I asked Claude (Opus 5.5 Medium running in regular Claude Chat) to port a Three.js Nudibranch‑themed Fabergé egg example to pure Vanilla JS/WebGL. Claude produced a working version, showing that the model can create 3D code without relying on Three.js.

🔍 Overview

  • Claude Opus 5.5 Medium was prompted to rewrite a Three.js scene in Vanilla JS.
  • The original Three.js egg file is 77 KB; the generated Vanilla JS version is 98 KB.
  • Claude’s output is not identical to the Three.js code, and the transcript notes a difference.
  • The author finds the Three.js version slightly easier to read but considers the difference minor.

🧩 How it worked

  • Prompt: “Port that to Vanilla JS, in the same thread where it had built it.”
  • Result: Claude returned a complete Vanilla JS/WebGL implementation (link provided in the evidence).
  • The transcript (linked) shows Claude’s comments explaining the differences.

⚙️ Key details

  • Capability confirmed: Claude Opus 5.5 can perform 3D modeling in Vanilla JS + WebGL without Three.js.
  • Code size comparison:
    • Three.js version: 77 KB
    • Vanilla JS version: 98 KB
  • Readability: Three.js code feels slightly easier to understand, but the author rarely examines the code for such projects.

🚀 Availability

  • The feature is accessible now in Claude Opus 5.5 Medium via the regular Claude Chat interface.

💡 Why it matters

  • Demonstrates that a large language model can generate functional WebGL graphics code without external 3D libraries.
  • Opens the possibility for developers to obtain lightweight, library‑free 3D demos directly from AI prompts.

#Claude #WebGL #VanillaJS #AIcoding

Source: Comment: The Web Is More Than Enough, by Paul Ford

item.title: Claude Opus 5.5 Optimizes SQLite C Extension Performance Beyond Rust Implementation
item.description:
Claude Opus 5.5 Optimizes SQLite C Extension Performance Beyond Rust Implementation

On November 8th, 2026, an investigation using the Claude Opus 5.5 model demonstrated the creation and optimization of a custom SQLite extension. The project focused on developing a parse_number() function to convert strings—such as currency and percentages—into numeric values that can be summed and sorted.

🔍 Overview

The parse_number(value) function was designed with specific parsing capabilities:

  • Strips symbols including ‘,’, ‘$’, ‘£’, and ‘%’.
  • Handles leading ‘-’ characters.
  • Returns ‘NULL’ for any values it cannot successfully parse.

⚙️ Key details

The development process compared building the extension in C versus Rust, revealing significant differences in file size and execution speed:

  • File Size: The C extension resulted in a 14 KB file, while Rust implementations were significantly larger at 321 KB (using Rusqlite) and 298 KB (using sqlite-loadable-rs).
  • Performance Optimization: Although the Rust version was initially faster due to its strtod equivalent being twice as fast as C’s, a custom C function written by the AI achieved superior speeds.

📊 Performance results

The following table displays the net cost per row measured over 2 million rows. Lower values indicate better performance.

Data Type Original C New C Rusqlite (Rust) sqlite-loadable (Rust)
Mixed data 67 ns 19 ns 46 ns 41 ns
Integers only 25 ns 16 ns 36 ns 32 ns
Decimals only 106 ns 18 ns 55 ns 47 ns

🚀 Availability

The final prototype was formatted as a research report for the simonw/research GitHub repository. The model provided the investigation as a downloadable zip file containing the necessary folder structure for the repository.

#SQLite #ClaudeAI #Programming #Rust #C

Source: Research: parse_number() as a SQLite extension: C vs Rust

item.title: Managing AI-Generated Pull Request Descriptions with HTML Details and Summary Tags
item.description:
Managing AI-Generated Pull Request Descriptions with HTML Details and Summary Tags

Developers are increasingly utilizing coding agents like Claude Code and Codex to open pull requests (PRs) and manage project changes. While these agents generate accurate and comprehensive descriptions—detailing the problem, the solution, and verification steps—the volume of text can be overwhelming, leading to the use of specific Markdown techniques to organize information for human reviewers.

🧩 How it works

GitHub Markdown supports the HTML <details><summary> elements, which render as a collapsed heading that can be expanded to view larger blocks of text. This feature allows developers to bundle agent-written content behind a concise, human-curated summary:

  • The <summary> tag serves as the clickable line of text that acts as a summary.
  • The <details> element wraps the rest of the content to keep it hidden until expanded.
  • A carefully selected opening paragraph provides a high-level explanation to get readers up to speed.
  • The full agent-written description is placed within the tags to prevent the reader’s eyes from glazing over.
  • Screenshots are sometimes included to quickly illustrate new features.

⚙️ Key details

To maintain clarity, the order of the tags can be remembered using the five-syllable mnemonic “details-summary.” Developers use the summary line to identify the source and intensity of the AI work.

Attribute Usage in PR Summary
Model Name Identifies the specific agent used, such as Claude Opus 5.5.
Effort Level Indicates the intensity of the work, such as “Medium”.
Human Judgement Used to select the short opener or extract a summary from the agent’s text.

💡 Why it matters

Using the <details><summary> structure ensures that the PR remains a functional unit of work for bundling commits and documenting decisions without sacrificing readability. It provides a promise to the reader that the visible text represents human judgment on what is worth their time, while keeping the exhaustive agent-generated verification steps and data accessible for those who need it.

#GitHub #AIagents #ClaudeCode #Markdown #PullRequests

Source: Hide your slop PR descriptions behind

item.title: BankAI Releases Intelligent Document Automation for Bank Statement Analysis and Querying
item.description:
BankAI Releases Intelligent Document Automation for Bank Statement Analysis and Querying

BankAI has introduced a full-stack system for automated bank statement processing, combining layout detection, optical character recognition, and local large language models. The platform enables users to extract, structure, analyze, and query financial data from PDFs through a secure, multi-agent architecture.

🔍 Overview

BankAI provides a comprehensive pipeline for financial intelligence, including income and expense categorization, trend analysis, and natural language querying. The system is designed with a local-first approach, prioritizing data privacy through PII redaction before embedding data into vector databases like Qdrant or Chroma. It supports advanced features such as reasoning model content handling and real-time GPU monitoring.

🧩 How it works

The system utilizes a multi-layered technical stack to process complex financial documents:

  • PDF Parsing: Employs YOLO layout detection, OCR, and LLM-based table extraction.
  • Agent Orchestration: Uses multiple harnesses including CrewAI, LangChain Deep Agents, and Hermes in a Docker sandbox.
  • Secure RAG Pipeline: Redacts personally identifiable information (PII) prior to vector database storage.
  • GPU Acceleration: Supports NVIDIA GPUs for PyTorch embeddings and LLM inference, offering significant performance improvements over CPU builds.
  • MCP Integration: Provides Claude Desktop and Cursor tools via the BankAI API using the MCP stdio standard.

⚙️ Key details

BankAI is built on a modern full-stack architecture with specific hardware and software recommendations for optimal performance.

Component Specification
Backend FastAPI, SQLAlchemy 2.0 (async), PostgreSQL 16, Celery
Frontend React SPA with REST authentication
LLM Inference vLLM, SGLang, Strata, LM Studio, Ollama via LiteLLM
Model Requirements Prefer 9B+ parameters, 16K+ context length (32K recommended)
Vector Database Qdrant, Chroma
Monitoring Prometheus + Grafana (DCGM + node-exporter) for GPU metrics
Output Formats Markdown reports (preferred), strict JSON via post-processing

🚀 Availability

The development environment includes a Jupyter notebook for CrewAI experimentation and MLflow integration to trace LLM calls and agent workflows. Additionally, the project provides a library of 2,954 everyday prompts available in both English and Chinese, covering domains such as coding, research, and marketing. Users can also access a directory of skills designed to extend Claude Code.

💡 Why it matters

By facilitating local LLM inference and reasoning-aware model support, BankAI allows organizations to process sensitive financial documents without relying on external cloud providers. The system’s ability to provide a nine-dimension audit with file-line evidence and machine-checkable verification gates supports complex coding and financial analysis tasks that require high precision and security.

#BankAI #DocumentAutomation #LLM #FinTech #AIagents #OpenSource

Source: johnsonhk88/AI-Bank-Statement-Document-Automation-By-LLM-And-Personal-Finanical-Analysis-Prediction Source: ai-boost/awesome-prompts

item.title: Open-source Hive runtime enables parallel AI agent colonies for business tasks
item.description:
Open-source Hive runtime enables parallel AI agent colonies for business tasks

Hive has been updated as an open-source runtime for colonies of AI agents designed to perform real business work. The system coordinates “queen” agents that manage parallel workers to complete complex tasks without the need for pre-wired workflow graphs.

🧩 How it works

Hive utilizes a hierarchical structure to manage business workflows as they unfold:

  • Initial Learning: A queen agent performs the first part of a job herself to learn the requirements, then saves the method as a reusable skill.
  • Colony Formation: After defining the method, the queen proposes a colony and assigns the remaining work to as many parallel worker agents as the task needs.
  • Shared Tracking: Every result is written to a shared tracker—a SQLite table on disk—rather than a context window. This allows the system to query, audit, and resume work.
  • Active Auditing: The queen checks every row of the tracker for accuracy. For example, in a research task, a queen can identify and clear incorrect entries recorded by workers before providing a final answer.

🔍 Overview

Queens are long-lived agents with specific roles, memory, and tools. Because the system shapes the colony dynamically, there is no fixed workflow graph to draw. The state of the work is maintained on disk, keeping track of what has been completed and what remains.

⚙️ Key details

The platform is designed to be compatible with a wide range of models and local configurations:

Feature Supported Options
LLM Providers Anthropic, OpenAI, Google Gemini, Groq, Cerebras, OpenRouter, Hive LLM
Local Models Ollama (requires no API key)
Security API keys stored encrypted under ~/.hive
Tools Quickstart installs uv and ripgrep if missing

🚀 Availability

Setting up Hive requires Python 3.11+, Node.js 20+, and git.

  • Installation: Users can run pip install "aden-hive[tools]" to install the runtime from PyPI.
  • Management: The command hive open builds and opens the dashboard at http://127.0.0.1:8787.
  • Development: Projects can be built on Hive’s agent loop by depending on the aden-hive package. Optional packages are also available for features such as chat-app channels.

#AIagents #OpenSource #Automation #Python #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: aden-hive/hive

item.title: NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Features Vera Rubin Support and Enhanced Multi-Process Service
item.description:
NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Features Vera Rubin Support and Enhanced Multi-Process Service

NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 has reached general availability, bringing the NVIDIA Vera Rubin architecture to enterprise production. This update provides new platform support, including Windows on Arm for DGX Station, and introduces advanced customization for GPU work scheduling through locality domains and Multi-Process Service (MPS) v3.

🔍 Overview

  • NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 achieves general availability (GA) across major new platforms.
  • NVIDIA Vera Rubin support has moved to GA, making it ready for enterprise production.
  • Windows on Arm support, which has been GA since CUDA 13.4, now extends to the NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows.
  • Enhanced GPU scheduling is introduced via locality domains and updated MPS controls.

⚙️ Key details

  • SM Resource Control: Applications can choose between uniform streaming multiprocessor (SM) partitions or utilize the cudaDevSmResourceGroupLocalityDomainSupplementalSms flag to include all available SMs in selected domains.
  • Driver Compatibility: Starting with the Rubin architecture, CUDA supports Windows Driver Display Model (WDDM) and Microsoft Compute Driver Model (MCDM), while Tesla Compute Cluster (TCC) is no longer supported.
  • CUDA Graph Enhancements: Support is added for batched 1D memory copies, enabling cudaMemcpyBatchAsync calls to be captured and replayed within reusable graph workflows.
  • CUDA Tile Kernels: Kernels can now perform direct multi-GPU communication and call SIMT library device functions from cuTile Python or CUDA Tile C++ on data already in registers or shared memory.

🧩 How it works

Feature Functionality
Weighted timeslicing Scales the base compute timeslice per MPS server to give longer compute turns to specific workloads.
SM partition load balancing Enables workloads to borrow capacity via --max-chunks and lend SMs when idle using --shareable=true.
Cgroup-based routing Maps cgroup v2 subtrees to MPS namespaces to route clients automatically through the daemon’s main socket.
Polling memory accounting Provides a fallback for usage and limit verification; forced via nvidia-cuda-mps-control memacct set force_polling=true.
Multi-GPU access Uses unicast pointers for NVLink-connected GPUs and multicast pointers for NVSwitch fabrics with NVLink SHARP support.

In addition to these features, applications can use discovery mode within the cudaDevSmResourceSplit() API to obtain partition SM counts. MPS v3 also ensures that borrowed resources are reclaimed before reassignment, while applications continue to see a stable base partition size.

🚀 Availability

  • Enterprise Production: NVIDIA Vera Rubin support is now in general availability.
  • Platform Extensions: Windows on Arm support is now available for NVIDIA DGX Station for Windows.

#CUDA #NVIDIA #VeraRubin #MPS #GPU

Source: NVIDIA CUDA 13.5 Brings NVIDIA Vera Rubin GA Support | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: New transformers-mic Standard Proposed to Detect Regressions Using Tiny Model Fixtures
item.description:
New transformers-mic Standard Proposed to Detect Regressions Using Tiny Model Fixtures

On July 30, 2026, an update to the Transformers library enabled PyTorch’s scaled dot-product attention (SDPA) for T5, which unintentionally allowed UMT5’s decoder to attend to future tokens during training. This bug remained in the main branch for nearly two months because existing integration tests often identify regressions only after they have been merged. To address this, a new standard called transformers-mic has been proposed to package tiny test models that can quickly and reliably flag such architectural regressions.

🔍 Overview

  • The July 2026 SDPA integration allowed UMT5 to peek at answers it was supposed to predict during training without causing a crash.
  • Transformers currently supports over 750 model types and runs more than 88,000 CPU tests and 200,000 daily GPU tests.
  • Scheduled integration tests that load real checkpoints and exercise APIs on real hardware may find regressions only after they are already in the main branch.

🧩 How it works

Transformers-mic is a proposed standard for packaging tiny test models, referred to as fixtures, to validate model integrity. A contract covers a specific architecture and a usage path, meaning compatible checkpoints can share a single fixture while maintaining their own expected results.

Component Function
MIC Fixture A reduced model that keeps layer kinds (MoE, sliding attention) but reduces hidden sizes and depth.
Contract Validates that running a usage path on a fixture produces the expected baselines.
Fleet Dataset Pins each MIC to a frozen revision on the Hub along with specific package versions.
Verification Checks training loss, finite gradients, and that weight changes occur after an optimizer step.

⚙️ Key details

  • Fixture Creation: Fixtures are built by starting from a real checkpoint and reducing hidden sizes, attention heads, and depth while preserving vocabulary, special tokens, and input dimensions.
  • Efficiency: In a study, a UMT5 fixture used only 66 MB of weights compared to the 1,227 MB source checkpoint.
  • Reproducibility: CI runs record the fleet revision used for later reproduction, and fixtures are reused rather than rebuilt for every pull request.
  • File Integrity: The process copies tokenizer and processor files byte for byte and maintains the original weights file format.

💡 Why it matters

The small UMT5 fixture successfully flagged the SDPA regression that lasted from July 30 to September 28. When tested, it showed label log-probabilities differed from the reviewed baseline by 1.22 and training loss by approximately 0.20. The selected T5 contract’s runner step took only 13.4 seconds on CPU, demonstrating that these contracts can provide rapid feedback that existing large-scale integration tests might delay.

#Transformers #PyTorch #MachineLearning #SoftwareTesting #OpenSource

Source: Transformers Model Integration Contracts

item.title: a2a-adapter Enables Easy A2A Protocol Integration for Local AI Agents
item.description:
a2a-adapter Enables Easy A2A Protocol Integration for Local AI Agents

The new a2a-adapter tool wraps existing agent CLIs, local agents, workflow engines, and Python agent frameworks behind the A2A (Agent-to-Agent) Protocol.

🔍 Overview

  • Provides automatic AgentCard generation, JSON‑RPC handling, task lifecycle management, and streaming via the official A2A SDK.
  • Your adapter only needs to invoke the underlying agent; a2a‑adapter takes care of the A2A plumbing.

🧩 How It Works

  1. Install a2a-adapter into your project’s virtual environment (Python 3.11+ required).
  2. Wrap your existing agent with the adapter and start the server.
  3. The adapter exposes the agent as an A2A server, e.g., http://localhost:9000, with an auto‑generated Agent Card at http://localhost:9000/.well-known/agent-card.json.
  4. The server can be mounted inside an existing ASGI app using to_a2a(adapter).

⚙️ Supported Agents

  • Claude Code
  • Codex
  • Pi
  • OpenClaw
  • n8n
  • LangGraph
  • LangChain
  • CrewAI
  • Ollama
  • Hermes Agent
  • Custom Python functions

🚀 Installation & Usage

  • Install the CLI as an isolated tool so the a2a-adapter command is on your PATH.
  • Upgrade later with uv tool upgrade a2a-adapter.
  • Avoid system‑wide pip install because macOS’s built‑in pip runs Python 3.9 (too old) and many Linux distributions block it (PEP 668).
  • Ensure the underlying agent works on its own; a2a-adapter does not install the agent.
    • Example: install Claude Code and run claude once to sign in.
  • If the agent executable is not on PATH, specify it with --executable /path/to/agent.
  • Start the server from the project directory where the agent should run.
  • Options placed before -- configure the A2A server; options placed after -- are passed to the underlying agent CLI.
  • Run a2a-adapter -help for a list of supported agents, or a2a-adapter <agent> -help for agent‑specific usage.

💡 Why It Matters

  • A single adaptor turns any compatible local agent into an A2A‑compliant service without modifying the agent code.
  • The same A2A server interface works for both classic local agents (Claude Code, Codex, Pi, OpenClaw) and modern Python‑based frameworks.
  • By providing a standard Agent Card at /.well-known/agent-card.json, the adapter enables discovery and integration in broader A2A ecosystems.

#A2A #AIAgents #Python #Tooling

Source: hybroai/a2a-adapter

item.title: Resolving Python 3.15 Dependency Errors Caused by Local uv.lock Files
item.description:
Resolving Python 3.15 Dependency Errors Caused by Local uv.lock Files

Switching to Python 3.15 can cause occasional dependency errors when local uv.lock files pin dependency versions that lack Python 3.15 wheels.

🔍 Overview

Running commands such as uv run pytest leaves uv.lock files in the local environment. Because these files are listed in .gitignore, they are not committed to repositories. However, they can cause build failures when the locked version of a dependency does not yet support Python 3.15.

⚙️ Key details

  • Library practices: Most library projects omit a uv.lock file so they do not lock dependency versions for downstream users.
  • Error cause: Running uv run pytest generates a local uv.lock file, which may pin a dependency version such as watchfiles==1.1.1 that lacks a Python 3.15 wheel.
  • Build failure error: A failure occurs during maturin.build_wheel because the configured Python interpreter version (3.15) is newer than PyO3’s maximum supported version (3.14).

💡 Resolution

When encountering this error, deleting the uv.lock file and running uv run pytest again usually fixes the problem.

#Python #uv #PyO3 #SoftwareDevelopment

Source: If in doubt, delete the uv.lock file

item.title: Kiro AI IDE and AWS Transform Enable Repeatable PHP‑to‑Java Migration
item.description:
Kiro AI IDE and AWS Transform Enable Repeatable PHP‑to‑Java Migration

A new AI‑enabled workflow lets teams move mature PHP applications to Java with a measurable, repeatable process.

🔍 Overview

  • “When your team moves a mature PHP application to Java, you gain stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling.”
  • “Kiro is an AI integrated development environment (IDE) that pairs an AI agent with your codebase to run multi‑step engineering tasks with you in the loop.”
  • “AWS Transform is the AWS agentic AI service for large‑scale migration and modernization, and it now integrates natively with Kiro.”

🧩 How it works

  • “The approach centers on a reusable engine: a shared methodology, a mechanical discovery scanner, and an eight‑phase workflow.”
  • “This engine treats the original PHP application as the specification and refuses to declare the Java port correct until a parity harness verifies it.”
  • “Everything here is packaged as skill files: versioned Markdown capability packages that encode the migration methodology (php-to-java-migration) and the discovery scanner workflow (php-model-discovery).”
  • “The engine is organized around a single principle: one shared brain, many projects.”
  • “At the top is a global .kiro/ layer that every project draws on.”
  • “A shared, global layer under .kiro/ holds two Skills, php-model-discovery (the scanner) and php-to-java-migration (the eight‑phase playbook), plus the core‑workflow.md Steering file.”

⚙️ Key details

  • “Kiro brings an AI agent into your editor to drive a migration step by step.”
  • “Open the repository root as a Kiro workspace and the skills activate automatically when you ask Kiro to migrate a PHP application.”
  • “Kiro then walks the eight‑phase workflow with explicit approval gates, so you review the discovery manifest, approve the rulebook, and sign off on each phase before the next begins.”
  • “Use Kiro to work through the code first: run the skill on one application, read the generated Java, and run the tests.”
  • “When you want to migrate more, AWS Transform runs the same methodology agentically with review at the checkpoints the skill defines.”
  • “Kiro handles one application at a time and suits first‑of‑a‑kind frameworks.”
  • “AWS Transform runs many applications as parallel jobs.”
  • “Both paths read the same skill files, so every rulebook fix made in Kiro improves the next AWS Transform run, and vice versa.”
  • “The scanner is discover‑models.php, a single‑file, dependency‑free PHP command‑line tool that doesn’t execute the target code.”
  • “It only reads source text as tokens, so it runs against apps of your choice whether its dependencies are installed.”
  • “Each per‑project folder holds its own PHP source, Java output, and spec sub‑folder under .kiro/specs/, so improving the methodology once lets every project inherit the gain.”

🚀 Availability

  • “You start with an open repository, so you can run the engine yourself rather than read about it.”
  • “Open the repository root as a Kiro workspace and the skills activate automatically when you ask Kiro to migrate a PHP application.”
  • “Through that integration, you can hand AWS Transform the same skill files that govern an interactive Kiro session, so discovery before translation, the parity harness as referee, and ‘fix the loop, not the code’ apply to an autonomous run.”

💡 Why it matters

  • Stronger type safety, broader library support, and more predictable scaling are achieved by moving to Java.
  • An eight‑phase, parity‑first pipeline guarantees that the Java port matches the original PHP specification before it is accepted.
  • The same skill files power both an interactive, single‑application workflow (Kiro) and a large‑scale, parallel workflow (AWS Transform), ensuring consistency across projects.

#PHP #Java #AI #Migration #AWS

Source: Build a repeatable PHP-to-Java migration engine with Kiro | Amazon Web Services

item.title: AnyLanguageModel adds on‑device speech and decision packages for Swift
item.description:
AnyLanguageModel adds on‑device speech and decision packages for Swift

Today the AnyLanguageModel project announced two new Swift packages — AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel — that extend its 1.x Swift API approach to speech transcription and decision‑making while keeping a familiar Apple‑style API.

🔍 Overview

  • AnySpeechRecognizer implements Apple’s new SpeechAnalyzer API but lets you pick the underlying engine, including NVIDIA’s Parakeet and Alibaba’s Qwen3‑ASR running locally via Core ML.
  • It adds speaker diarization to track who is speaking when.
  • AnyDecisionModel answers yes‑or‑no, multiple‑choice, and rating‑scale questions, returning typed results and probabilities derived from model logits rather than generated text.
  • Both packages can download open models from the Hugging Face Hub and run them entirely on‑device.

🗣️ AnySpeechRecognizer

  • Mirrors Apple’s SpeechAnalyzer, SpeechTranscriber, DictationTranscriber, SpeechDetector, and AssetInventory components.
  • Uses Apple’s Speech framework as the default engine; swapping to a different engine only requires changing the import.
  • Supports file‑based and live audio input, volatile results, word timing, and confidence scores when the selected engine provides them.
  • Includes built‑in speaker diarization.

🤖 AnyDecisionModel

  • Provides typed answers (yes/no, multiple‑choice, rating‑scale) with associated probabilities.
  • Derives answers from model probabilities, not from text generation.
  • Runs on‑device with MLX, Core AI, llama.cpp, or a decision model from Jev or Ollama.
  • Can be integrated with the same Swift API style used for language and speech models.

📦 Model Options

Model Size(s) Languages / Dialects Notable Traits
Parakeet v3 (NVIDIA) 0.6 B 25 European languages (auto‑detect locale) Runs on Core ML runtime, supports file & live input, volatile results, word timing, confidence
Parakeet Ultra (Moondream) 0.6 B (post‑trained) Same as v3 More accurate in most measurements
Parakeet Unified (NVIDIA) – English only –
Qwen3‑ASR (Alibaba) 0.6 B, 1.7 B 30 languages + 22 Chinese dialects (Mandarin, Cantonese, Japanese, Korean) Provides a single final result per ≤40 s segment, no volatile results, no word timing or confidence, runs on GPU, slower than Parakeet, better for file transcription

⚙️ How it works

  • You create a SpeechAnalyzer (or AnySpeechRecognizer) and attach modules such as SpeechTranscriber and SpeechDetector.
  • Provide an audio file or a stream of audio buffers; results are delivered via asynchronous sequences as they become available.
  • AssetInventory handles model installation; downloads occur only when the app requests them.
  • Models are stored in the standard Hugging Face cache, allowing a macOS app outside the sandbox to share them with Python or other Hugging Face tools.

🚀 Availability

  • Packages are available as Swift packages; they depend on the 1.x releases of AnyLanguageModel and swift‑huggingface.
  • Approximate download sizes (per model):
    • Parakeet variants: ~600 MB each + ~590 MB for the live encoder.
    • Qwen3‑ASR: 0.9 GB to 2.4 GB depending on model size.
    • Sortformer (used for speaker diarization): ~250 MB.
  • Once downloaded, models run entirely on‑device, with no ongoing cloud usage required.

#Swift #SpeechRecognition #OnDeviceAI #MachineLearning

Source: Introducing AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel: Open Models for Speech and Decisions on Apple Platforms
